plan: Final experiment design delivered as a single document. Section 0 pre-registers five hypotheses (H1 SSP lowers ASR under prompt-level attacks; H2 same under token-level, conditional on open models; H3 SSP does not cost >X pp utility; H4 the effect is attributable to safety content, not any system prompt; H5 effect transfers across model families). Section 1 operationalizes the research question, fixing the alphabet (SSP, Without SSP, ASR, token- vs prompt-level). Section 2 records the six approved defaults: Branch B+C (two open families + closed-API + chat-template control); multi-turn subsumed under prompt-level with its own row; three SSP variants (SSP-A short imperative, SSP-B policy paragraph, SSP-C matched-length paraphrase); 50 prompts × 3 seeds per cell; LLM-judge + strict-regex co-primary; token-level execution assumed external ≥A100 outside the sandbox. Section 3 pins three target models: Open-A Llama-3-class, Open-B Qwen/Mistral-class, a closed-API GPT-4-class reference, plus a Branch-C chat-template control cell on Open-A. Section 4 catalogs token-level attacks (GCG/PEZ/GBDA/AutoDAN) and prompt-level attacks (DAN persona, base64/rot13/translation obfuscation, persuasion, cipher/code, many-shot, Crescendo) with budgets. Section 5 fixes corpora (HarmBench primary, JailbreakBench as held-out transfer, MMLU/IFEval/AlpacaEval for utility). Section 6 specifies five system-prompt levels (none, neutral="You are a helpful assistant.", SSP-A, SSP-B, SSP-C) plus a frozen decoding policy (greedy primary, sampled sensitivity). Section 7 lays out the cell matrix showing which (model × level × SSP) cells are eligible. Section 8 makes ASR-composite the primary endpoint (regex ∧ judge agree) and adds RR, over-refusal, utility, multi-seed consistency, cost-to-success. Section 9 lists ten controls including paraphrase, presence-control, benign cells, decoding, transfer probes, judge calibration, frozen pre-registration. Section 10 is the analysis plan: stratified permutation tests, Bonferroni–Holm correction, Cohen's h effect sizes, content-vs-presence decomposition for H4, cross-family correlation for H5, a pre-registered asymmetric "median ΔASR" test, and an explicit "what counts as SSP helps" decision rule. Section 11 fixes a dual threat model (TM1 textual leakage vs TM2 functional harm). Section 12 details feasibility: nothing runs inside this sandbox (no GPU, no network, no torch/transformers); token-level cells require external GPU; prompt-level cells require external API access; provides an ordered budget-trimming rule if forced. Section 13 freezes the pre-registration contract. Section 14 is the risk register and falsifiability rules. Three appendices hold placeholder SSP-A/B/C, the judge rubric, and the attack implementation catalog. The document does not invent execution results or ASR numbers.

context.question: Does incorporating a Safety System Prompt (SSP) significantly enhance the robustness of Large Language Models (LLMs) against jailbreak attacks? Specifically, how does the presence of SSP influence the Attack Success Rate (ASR) under both token-level and prompt-level attacks?
